title: Mistakes Were Made, But Not By Me

questions.q: Why do people find it so hard to admit a mistake, according to the summary?
a: It clashes with the way they see themselves
They fear legal consequences more than the truth
They usually forget the details of what happened
They assume everyone else makes the same errors
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines cognitive dissonance as conflict between two ideas about who you are.

questions.q: What do smokers in the summary do instead of admitting their addiction?
a: They tell themselves they do not smoke that much
They avoid the topic of smoking entirely
They blame tobacco companies in public
They quit only when friends pressure them
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the smoker's excuse as an example of self-justification.

questions.q: What does the pyramid of choice illustrate?
a: Justifying a choice makes you surer it was right
People copy the morals of those around them
Most people steal when nobody is watching
Morals are fixed before a person reaches adulthood
questions.why: Lesson 2 says each person descends a narrowing path and grows more certain of their own morality.

questions.q: How did Chinese and Japanese classrooms handle a student's math mistake?
a: The student retried at the board with class support
The student was moved to an easier group
The mistake was corrected privately after school
The whole class was given extra homework
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the weakest student reworked the problem in front of everyone until getting it right.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest focusing criticism on?
a: Behavior rather than who someone is
Character rather than outcomes
Results rather than intentions
Effort rather than ability
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to critique actions, not identity, to build a growth mindset around mistakes.
